summary: Kōdō Yamada (1868–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held teaching posts at Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kōdō Yotsuya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MA at Komazawa University and a PhD from the University of Hamburg.
Kōichi Kozaka (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Hakuyu Hadano and served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University, where his post is attested in 1991.

L. A. Ravi Varma (1884–1958) was an Indology scholar who studied at Madras Medical College. Around 1938 to 1944, he served as Honorary Director of the Oriental Manuscripts Department at the University of Kerala.

L. Carrington Goodrich (1894–1986) worked in Sinology and history and archaeology. Educated at Chefoo School and Williams College (~1913–1917), he served as Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University (~1945–1961).

L. P. N. Perera worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as supervisor at Vidyodaya Campus, head of the Post Graduate Institute of Buddhist Studies at Vidyalankara Campus, and Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Lajos Ligeti (1902–1987) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and Paris under Pelliot, Maspero, and Bacot, he held chairs at Pázmány Péter Catholic University and Eötvös Loránd University.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Lakshmanacharya was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held teaching posts at Shri Ramanuja Pathashala in Mathura, attested in 1889 and 1900.

Lal Mani Joshi (1935–1984), a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology, earned degrees from Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur. He held posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, Amherst, Haverford, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indology scholar who served as Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Baroda and held a post attested in 1939 at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.

Lama Jampa Thaye (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a PhD at the University of Manchester, studied with several Tibetan masters, and joined the faculty of the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche (born 1935) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ngor Monastery, held the post of Thartse Shabthung there in 1959, and founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

Lama Palden Drolma specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She received training from traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche, among others.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.

Lambert Schmithausen (born 1939) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. He held associate professorship at Münster (1970–1973) and the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University by 1986 and served as a professor at the University of San Diego (attested 1997).

Lance S. Cousins (1942–2015) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Cambridge. He taught at Manchester (~1970–2000) and Oxford (~2000–2015), served as Fellow at Wolfson College, and was President of the Pali Text Society (2002–2003).
Lang Chen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed a PhD at Yale University (attested 2015) supervised by Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff, and also studied under Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Temple University, where she studied under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert Max Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.
